changes.previous: Lean for biology: turn a scientific claim into a precise statement that people and machines can check.
changes.replacement: Lean for biology: make scientific claims precise enough for people and machines to check.

changes.previous: Lean for biology is the foundation: mathematical claims with explicit assumptions and machine-checkable consequences.
changes.replacement: Lean for biology: mathematical claims, explicit assumptions, machine-checkable consequences.

changes.previous: Formalize that knowledge, and new capabilities become possible: reusable constraints, compatible models, candidate designs and experiments that target the missing evidence.
changes.replacement: Formalized knowledge enables reusable constraints, compatible models, candidate designs and experiments aimed at missing evidence.

changes.previous: Our test case is a fish that could glide, starting from zebrafish. Published fin-growth genetics and natural flying-fish measurements help frame the design.
changes.replacement: Our test case asks whether zebrafish-inspired fin designs could glide. Published fin-growth genetics and flying-fish measurements frame it.

changes.previous: We formalized a fin-beam stiffness condition that bounds deflection. Lean compiled the theorem and rejected a corrupted law. Two computations reused a versioned mechanics claim; independent review preserved both the numerical checks and questions about biological relevance.
changes.replacement: Lean compiled a fin-beam stiffness bound and rejected a corrupted law. Two computations reused a versioned mechanics claim; independent review kept numerical checks alongside biological questions.

changes.previous: The studio spans sequence candidates, bioelectric models, fin mechanics, aerodynamics and collective behavior. Each layer exposes equations, controls and evidence. Virtual instruments show model-specific predictions, not measurements.
changes.replacement: The studio links sequence candidates, bioelectricity, mechanics, aerodynamics and collective behavior. Equations, controls, evidence and virtual instruments expose model predictions, not measurements.

changes.previous: The ambition is a biological compiler: candidate DNA, a build plan and a validation strategy. Our current compiler checks linked artifacts and identifies unresolved interfaces.
changes.replacement: The biological compiler aims to output candidate DNA, a build plan and validation strategy. Today it checks linked artifacts and exposes missing interfaces.

changes.previous: Like AlphaFold predictions, computational candidates are hypotheses to test. We combine formal checks, numerical controls and observations, then use failures to guide the next experiment.
changes.replacement: Like AlphaFold predictions, candidates need testing. Formal checks, numerical controls and observations turn failures into targeted experiments.

changes.previous: Through MCP, people and agents can contribute, challenge and reuse that work. The flying fish is one example. The larger goal is a shared, checkable foundation for engineering biology.
changes.replacement: MCP lets people and agents contribute, challenge and reuse exact work. The flying fish is one test of a shared, checkable foundation for engineering biology.
